facts.statement: At least 37 incomplete fossils of Shonisaurus popularis were found in the Luning Formation of Nevada.
facts.quote: At least 37 incomplete fossil specimens of the type species, Shonisaurus popularis, have been found in the Luning Formation of Nevada, United States.

facts.statement: Fossils of Shonisaurus were first discovered in a large deposit in Nevada in 1920.
facts.quote: Fossils of Shonisaurus were first found in a large deposit in Nevada in 1920.

facts.statement: The name Shonisaurus means "lizard from the Shoshone Mountains" and refers to the formation where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: These were named Shonisaurus, which means "lizard from the Shoshone Mountains", after the formation where the fossils were found.

facts.statement: Shonisaurus popularis was adopted as the state fossil of Nevada in 1984.
facts.quote: S. popularis, was adopted as the state fossil of Nevada in 1984.

facts.statement: The genus Shonisaurus was named by Charles Camp in 1976.
facts.quote: It was named by Charles Camp in 1976.

facts.statement: A second species, Shonisaurus sikanniensis, was named in 2004 from fossils found in the Pardonet Formation of British Columbia.
facts.quote: A second species from the Pardonet Formation of British Columbia was named Shonisaurus sikanniensis in 2004.

facts.statement: A 2011 study suggested that Shonisaurus sikanniensis might actually be a species of Shastasaurus rather than Shonisaurus.
facts.quote: However, a phylogenetic study by Sander and colleagues in 2011 later showed S. sikanniensis to be a species of Shastasaurus rather than Shonisaurus.

facts.statement: Later studies have supported both hypotheses regarding the classification of Shonisaurus sikanniensis, with some authors placing it in Shonisaurus and others in Shastasaurus.
facts.quote: Support for both hypotheses has been found in later studies, with some authors classifying the species in Shonisaurus and others in Shastasaurus.

facts.statement: Shonisaurus popularis had a skull about 2.75 meters long and measured between 13.5 and 15 meters in total length.
facts.quote: With a large skull about 2.75 m long, S. popularis measured around 13.5 - 15 m in length and 21.6 - 29.7 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: Shonisaurus had a long snout and flippers that were much longer and narrower than those of other ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: Shonisaurus had a long snout, and its flippers were much longer and narrower than in other ichthyosaurs.

facts.statement: Recent findings indicate that Shonisaurus possessed teeth in all stages of growth, contrary to earlier reports of socketed teeth only in juveniles.
facts.quote: More recent finds however indicate that Shonisaurus possessed teeth in all ontogenetic stages.

facts.statement: Studies since the early 1990s show that Shonisaurus had a much more slender body than traditionally thought, though it was relatively deep compared to related marine reptiles.
facts.quote: studies of its body shape since the early 1990s have shown that the body was much more slender than traditionally thought, and had a relatively deep body compared with related marine reptiles.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Shonisaurus possessed a dorsal fin, as there is no solid evidence that it or other shastasaurids had this feature.
facts.quote: Shonisaurus también se la ha restaurado con una aleta dorsal, una característica hallada en ictiosaurios más avanzados. Sin embargo, no existe evidencia sólida de que Shonisaurus o alguna especie de los shastasáuridos poseyera una aleta dorsal.

facts.statement: The large tail fin typically reconstructed for Shonisaurus was likely not as developed as that of later ichthyosaur species, which had a tail profile more similar to sharks.
facts.quote: De la misma forma, la gran aleta caudal con que se ha reconstruido habitualmente probablemente no estaba tan desarrollada como las de especies de ictiosaurios posteriores, que tenían un perfil más similar a la de los tiburones.

facts.statement: An ichthyosaur found in the Himalayas called Himalayasaurus might be the same animal as Shonisaurus.
facts.quote: Un ictiosaurio encontrado en los montes Himalayas llamado Himalayasaurus, podría ser el mismo animal que Shonisaurus.

facts.statement: Shonisaurus is classified within the family Shastasauridae.
The genus authority for Shonisaurus is Camp, 1976.
Shonisaurus lived from the Carnian to the Rhaetian stages, between 233.6 and 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Rhaetian (233.6 to 201.4 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The Luning Formation where Shonisaurus fossils were found dates to the Late Triassic, around 227 million years ago.
rejected.quote: This formation dates to the late Carnian-early Norian age of the Late Triassic, around 227 million years ago.

rejected.statement: Excavations began thirty years after the initial discovery, uncovering the remains of 37 very large ichthyosaurs.
rejected.quote: Thirty years later, they were excavated, uncovering the remains of 37 very large ichthyosaurs.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'uncovering the remains of 37 very large ichthyosaurs'

rejected.statement: Shonisaurus sikanniensis was one of the largest marine reptiles of all time, reaching 21 meters in length and weighing 81.5 metric tons.
rejected.quote: S. sikanniensis was one of the largest marine reptiles of all time, measuring 21 m long and weighing 81.5 MT.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'sikanniensis was one of the largest marine reptiles'

rejected.statement: Evidence from teeth and gut contents indicates Shonisaurus was a raptorial predator that fed on vertebrates and shelled mollusks like cephalopods.
rejected.quote: Robust sectorial teeth and gut contents indicate that Shonisaurus was a macrophagous raptorial predator which fed on vertebrates and shelled mollusks like cephalopods, possibly even large-bodied prey.
